note: Gibraltar, since the UK–EU treaty arrangements took effect on 15 July 2026: there are no immigration controls between Gibraltar and the Schengen Area, so nationals of the EU, the EEA and Switzerland enter freely (taken as free movement); Gibraltar aligns its short-stay visa policy with Schengen's (90 days in any 180), so the nationals of the third countries the Government's list names enter without a visa, and every other third-country national needs a Schengen short-stay visa (issued by Spain where Gibraltar is the main destination). British citizens are home. UK visas and UK-residence exemptions no longer admit anyone.

sources.title: HM Government of Gibraltar, Press Release 558/2026, Technical Notice: Reminder Concerning Visa Arrangements (15 July 2026)
sources.said: As is the case between all Schengen states, Gibraltar has agreed to align its short stay visa policy (for stays of 90 days in any 180 days) with that of the Schengen Area. ... this is a necessary element of the treaty which allows for there to be no immigration controls between Gibraltar and the Schengen Area. ... Gibraltar will no longer operate exemptions linked to a person’s immigration status in the UK ... In addition to fulfilling other entry conditions applicable, such persons will be required to be in possession of a Schengen short-stay visa.
